why_math: Local geometric complexity varies spatially, so allocating network depth proportionally—more computation to complex regions, less to simple ones—eliminates wasted evaluation while maintaining accuracy everywhere.

Treating orientation fields as hard constraints rather than soft preferences forces the toolpath to respect the design intent exactly; the system then reports infeasibility rather than deforming the design.

Breaking scene generation into sequential stages (quantity→size→relations→placement) mirrors how humans design; each stage constrains the next, reducing entropy so every substage becomes more learnable than the joint problem.

A bijection between surfaces defines a unique mapping surface in the product space; minimizing its area via the Ginzburg-Landau functional automatically enforces bijectivity because no area-minimizing map can fold over itself.

Mixed discretization separates velocity from strain, forming a symmetric system that remains well-posed even when material stiffness is extreme, avoiding the tiny-timestep penalty that standard formulations require.

SPAD counts are quantized and nonlinear, but averaging many independent photon arrivals converges to the true spectrum by the law of large numbers; error shrinks exponentially as measurement count grows.

Explicitly tracking correspondence between medial-axis vertices and surface regions throughout simplification preserves the symmetry relationship that makes the medial axis a faithful shape descriptor.

LLMs encode rich real-world knowledge of material tactile properties and object affordances learned from training data, enabling them to match virtual properties to physical proxies via multimodal reasoning.

Neural basis functions inherit geometric properties (linearity, locality, smoothness, equivariance) from the Catmull-Clark base surface they offset, enabling direct real-time manipulation without retraining.

Splitting the domain into small subregions makes Monte Carlo walks short with controlled variance; assembling local solutions deterministically trades stochastic noise for a fixed discretization bias that is stable and reusable.

Lifting scalar task losses into high-dimensional ray-level residuals (GTRA) provides enough constraints to make the optical parameter space well-conditioned, allowing robust pseudo-second-order optimization where first-order fails.
MLLMs embed learned knowledge of how agents with different narrative roles move and interact, so conditioning on role description generates spatially consistent behaviors aligned with that role.

Representing shape, skeleton, and skin as mutually consistent S3 fields over shared space ensures topological consistency; confidence-decaying skeleton fields handle the geometric ambiguity at Voronoi boundaries where bone assignment is undefined.

Training a delighting network as a prior constrains the underdetermined inverse rendering problem (reflectance plus unknown light); the learned prior encodes that delighting principles generalize across heterogeneous datasets.

Progressive relaxation of the feasibility region (thickness parameter) allows the cage to escape local minima; QEM constraints prevent degeneracy, balancing simplicity and tightness via scheduled feasibility throughout optimization.
